title.en: JANUS Connection Scan — Relation-Specific Survival and Controlled Rewiring
title.ru: JANUS Connection Scan — устойчивость конкретной связи и контролируемое переподключение

scan_scope: selected Tranception, Dougan, SCOBY, Cardputer, signal, protection and proof-carrying records

primary_hidden_node_candidate.name: RELATION_SPECIFIC_SURVIVAL
primary_hidden_node_candidate.definition: A candidate connection is more informative when it survives context blinding but collapses when the specific relationship-bearing structure is deliberately rewired while preserving matched low-level statistics.
primary_hidden_node_candidate.core_question: Can JANUS destroy the detected relation without destroying the general statistical shape of the data?

emergent_invariants.name: RELATION_SPECIFICITY
emergent_invariants.description: A stronger candidate connection should depend on a specific relational arrangement rather than only on generic record statistics.

emergent_invariants.name: STATISTICAL_SHAPE_PRESERVATION
emergent_invariants.description: A useful rewiring null should preserve broad structural properties while selectively disrupting the hypothesized edge or topology.

emergent_invariants.name: BLINDING_PLUS_REWIRING
emergent_invariants.description: Survival under metadata blinding is stronger when paired with loss under relation-specific rewiring.

emergent_invariants.name: NULL_ALIGNMENT
emergent_invariants.description: If the real and rewired/null datasets lose or retain connections at similar rates, the candidate may be too generic to be informative.

emergent_invariants.name: EDGE_LEVEL_FALSIFICATION
emergent_invariants.description: The connection layer should expose a direct destructive test for the relation itself whenever the source representation permits one.

connections.machine_observation: A candidate operator is not enough; the specific relational arrangement should be testable by controlled rewiring that preserves low-level structure.
connections.pattern_description: The strongest machine-discovered relation is one that is blind-stable but relation-fragile.
alternative_explanations: Rewiring may remove meaningful causal structure rather than merely the hypothesized relation.
A candidate relation may be genuinely invariant to the chosen rewiring scheme.
connections.falsification_route: Construct a relation-specific rewiring null preserving schema, field counts, marginal distributions and where possible node degrees; compare edge survival against the untouched data.

connections.machine_observation: The next null must preserve the non-relational distributional structure strongly enough that a lost edge can be attributed to relation destruction rather than wholesale data corruption.
connections.pattern_description: Null construction itself becomes part of Connection validity: destroy the relationship, not the surrounding statistical world.
alternative_explanations: No rewiring scheme can preserve every property simultaneously.
Preserving the wrong low-level statistics may still create an unrepresentative null.
connections.falsification_route: Report a battery of preserved properties and quantify the divergence between real and rewired data before interpreting edge loss.

connections.machine_observation: Context-blinding removes several common detector dependencies, while rewiring offers a separate test of whether the relation itself carries signal.
connections.pattern_description: A candidate that survives metadata/context blinding and then collapses under targeted relation destruction has passed two different dependency challenges.
alternative_explanations: The two controls may share hidden assumptions about representation.
A relation can disappear under rewiring for reasons unrelated to the proposed interpretation.
connections.falsification_route: Cross the controls factorially: visible/blind × original/rewired, and inspect interaction effects instead of using a single comparison.

connections.machine_observation: Cross-domain operator recurrence is only informative if relation-specific controls behave differently from within-family schema recurrence.
connections.pattern_description: A relation should remain detectable across independent source families yet remain sensitive to rewiring within each family.
alternative_explanations: Cross-family recurrence may reflect the common archive schema rather than a domain-independent operator.
Rewiring may be feasible in one domain but meaningless in another.
connections.falsification_route: Define domain-appropriate relation destruction procedures and compare cross-family versus within-family survival using matched nulls.

connections.machine_observation: Connection currently contains falsification routes at the record level, but a stronger architecture is possible in which each individual edge has a defined relation-specific destructive control.
connections.pattern_description: The connection itself becomes an experimental object: identify the edge, define how to break it, and check whether the detector stops seeing it while controls remain intact.
alternative_explanations: Not every semantic connection has a meaningful rewiring operation.
Some relations are historical or symbolic and require different falsification procedures.
connections.falsification_route: Require every promoted Connection either to provide a relation-specific destructive test or explicitly document why such a test is undefined.

relation_specific_graph.candidate_hidden_path: REAL_SOURCE -> MINIMAL_CORE -> CANDIDATE_EDGE -> BLINDING -> REWIRE_EDGE -> compare survival
relation_specific_graph.critical_prediction: A genuinely relation-specific Connection should survive contextual blinding but lose detection under at least one well-matched relation-destroying intervention.
relation_specific_graph.counter_prediction: If the candidate survives aggressive rewiring or is equally common in the matched null, the relation may be too generic or detector-induced.

next_scan_strategy.name: RELATION_LEVEL_NULL_AND_REWIRE_BENCHMARK
next_scan_strategy.target: Move from identifying candidate relations to testing whether each relation has a measurable destructive boundary.
next_scan_strategy.promotion_rule: Do not promote a Connection beyond DISCOVERED unless it survives appropriate blinding, exceeds a matched null, and where structurally meaningful shows sensitivity to a relation-specific destructive control.

canonical_rule: The strongest machine-discovered connection is not merely one that survives analysis. It is one that survives the removal of explanations for its visibility and fails when the relationship itself is deliberately broken.
